actor: social service agency / health system / community organization
barrier_addressed: difficulty affording food, housing, health care, or other essentials
description: Screen for eligibility and connect households with food, housing, health coverage, and other income-support programs.

intervention_name: Income-support policies and refundable tax credits
barrier_addressed: insufficient household income
description: Use income-support policies that increase disposable household resources and reduce poverty-related barriers to health needs.

intervention_name: Affordable child care and work-support services
barrier_addressed: caregiving costs that limit employment
description: Expand affordable child care and related work supports so caregivers can maintain employment and household stability.

barrier_addressed: skills mismatch or limited job readiness
description: Provide vocational training, skills development, and job-placement support targeted to unemployed or underemployed adults.

barrier_addressed: difficulty finding and navigating employment opportunities
description: Pair career counseling with job-search assistance and placement support.

barrier_addressed: educational barriers to stable employment
description: Support completion of education, credentials, and training linked to employment opportunities.

barrier_addressed: rent burden and inability to maintain stable housing
description: Provide financial assistance that reduces rent burden and helps low-income households maintain stable housing.

barrier_addressed: difficulty locating and accessing housing supports
description: Help households identify affordable housing, complete applications, and connect with rental-assistance programs.

barrier_addressed: shortage of affordable stable housing
description: Increase the supply and affordability of stable housing through public investment and housing policy.

barrier_addressed: food affordability
description: Screen for eligibility and connect eligible households to nutrition benefits that improve purchasing power for food.

barrier_addressed: unrecognized food insecurity and fragmented referrals
description: Screen for food insecurity and connect patients with food banks, benefits, and community food resources.

intervention_name: Produce prescription or fruit-and-vegetable voucher program
barrier_addressed: cost of nutritious food
description: Provide eligible people with produce prescriptions or vouchers redeemable for fruits and vegetables.

intervention_name: Community food pantry or low-cost food access
barrier_addressed: insufficient household food supply
description: Connect households with local food banks, pantries, and low-cost food programs.

intervention_name: Expand healthy-food retail and redemption options
actor: public health agency / retailer / farmers market
barrier_addressed: few affordable healthy-food purchasing options
description: Expand affordable places to buy nutritious food, including grocery stores, farmers markets, mobile markets, and online redemption options.

intervention_name: Mobile markets or community food retail access
barrier_addressed: geographic distance from nutritious food
description: Bring affordable nutritious foods closer to underserved communities through mobile markets or expanded retail access.

actor: public health agency / retailer / community partners
barrier_addressed: healthy options do not match community preferences or needs
description: Design food-access programs with community partners so healthy foods are affordable, available, and culturally preferred.

intervention_name: Connected sidewalks, trails, and bicycle infrastructure
barrier_addressed: unsafe or disconnected routes
description: Improve pedestrian and bicycle transportation systems and connect them with everyday destinations.

intervention_name: Improve access to parks, trails, and recreation facilities
barrier_addressed: lack of convenient places to be active
description: Create, improve, or connect parks, trails, greenways, and recreation facilities so activity is easier and more accessible.

actor: school district / transportation agency / local government
barrier_addressed: safety and transportation barriers
description: Use safe walking and biking routes, crossings, traffic calming, and supportive programming to make active travel practical.

intervention_name: Recreation access plus outreach and programming
barrier_addressed: facilities exist but are hard to use or underused
description: Pair access to places for activity with classes, outreach, and programming that helps residents use them.

intervention_name: Walking groups or activity buddy programs
barrier_addressed: lack of social support or motivation
description: Create walking groups, buddy systems, or other social-support structures that help people maintain activity goals.

barrier_addressed: lack of feedback, goal tracking, or accountability
description: Combine an activity monitor with counseling, education, goal setting, and feedback rather than simply recommending exercise.

barrier_addressed: difficulty starting and sustaining regular activity
description: Use recurring coaching sessions with personalized activity and diet goals, progress tracking, and maintenance support.

barrier_addressed: unsafe, disconnected, or inconvenient places to walk or bike
description: Change transportation and land-use environments so walking and cycling become safe, practical ways to reach everyday destinations.

barrier_addressed: cost and lack of insurance
description: Help people obtain and keep health coverage and understand financial assistance so cost is less likely to delay care.

intervention_name: Connect patients with a usual source of primary care
barrier_addressed: no regular clinician or fragmented care
description: Link patients to a consistent primary-care clinician or practice for prevention, diagnosis, and chronic-disease management.

barrier_addressed: distance, transportation, time, or rural access
description: Offer evidence-based prevention services remotely when distance or local availability limits participation.

actor: community health worker / health system / public health agency
barrier_addressed: language, trust, navigation, and access barriers
description: Use community health workers to provide culturally appropriate outreach, navigation, coaching, enrollment support, and links between community and clinical services.

intervention_name: Structured diet and physical-activity prevention program
actor: trained lifestyle coach / health system / community program
barrier_addressed: need for sustained behavior-change support
description: Use a multi-session program with coaching, diet goals, physical-activity goals, and ongoing support for people at increased risk of type 2 diabetes.

intervention_name: Dietitian or nutrition counseling with individualized goals
barrier_addressed: generic nutrition advice does not fit individual needs
description: Provide tailored nutrition counseling, goal setting, and follow-up rather than one-time advice.

intervention_name: Produce access paired with nutrition education
actor: health system / public health agency / retailer
barrier_addressed: healthy food is unaffordable and skills/support are limited
description: Pair financial access to nutritious foods with practical education on shopping, preparation, and nutrition.

intervention_name: Intensive lifestyle-change program for diabetes prevention
barrier_addressed: need for sustained weight-management support
description: Use sustained diet, activity, coaching, and weight-management support for people at increased risk of type 2 diabetes.

barrier_addressed: one-size-fits-all weight advice
description: Set realistic weight goals and provide ongoing nutrition, activity, and behavioral support based on the person's circumstances.

barrier_addressed: difficulty sustaining behavior change alone
description: Provide ongoing peer or coaching support around activity, eating patterns, and realistic weight goals.

barrier_addressed: modifiable metabolic risk factors
description: Use a structured lifestyle program that improves weight, activity, diet, and blood-glucose risk factors among people at increased diabetes risk.

intervention_name: Clinician evaluation for metformin in appropriate high-risk patients
barrier_addressed: high diabetes risk despite or alongside lifestyle efforts
evidence_rating: NIDDK evidence-based option for selected patients
description: For selected people at high risk, clinicians may consider metformin alongside lifestyle intervention based on individual risk and clinical factors.

intervention_name: Refer to a structured diabetes-prevention lifestyle program
barrier_addressed: prediabetes or elevated glucose without structured prevention support
description: Refer eligible people with elevated glucose or high diabetes risk to a structured, evidence-based lifestyle-change program.

barrier_addressed: difficulty maintaining diet, activity, and weight goals
description: Use recurring contact, goal tracking, and feedback to support sustained prevention behavior.

actor: diabetes care and education specialist / health system
barrier_addressed: difficulty managing daily diabetes care
description: Provide personalized education and support for healthy eating, activity, medication use, glucose monitoring, problem solving, and reducing complication risk.

barrier_addressed: fragmented management of glucose, blood pressure, lipids, and medications
description: Use a multidisciplinary team that includes the patient, primary-care provider, and other professionals such as nurses, pharmacists, or dietitians.

barrier_addressed: need for sustained support with diet, activity, and weight management
description: Provide repeated counseling, coaching, and individualized guidance for diet and physical activity.

barrier_addressed: navigation, adherence, social-support, and access barriers
description: Use community health workers for education, coaching, care coordination, medication support, and culturally appropriate self-management assistance.

barrier_addressed: preventable eye, kidney, nerve, foot, and cardiovascular complications
description: Combine glucose, blood pressure, and cholesterol management with recommended eye, kidney, and foot monitoring and preventive care.

intervention_name: Self-measured blood pressure monitoring with clinical support
barrier_addressed: unrecognized or poorly tracked blood pressure
description: Use a validated home blood pressure monitor and share readings with a care team so treatment can be adjusted using measurements from daily life.

intervention_name: Team-based care for blood pressure control
barrier_addressed: fragmented follow-up and treatment adjustment
description: Use coordinated care in which clinicians, nurses, pharmacists, and other team members share responsibility for monitoring and improving blood pressure control.

barrier_addressed: medication access, adherence, or treatment-intensification barriers
description: Involve pharmacists in medication review, adherence support, blood pressure monitoring, and communication with the prescribing care team.

intervention_name: DASH-style eating pattern and sodium reduction
barrier_addressed: high sodium intake and dietary patterns that raise blood pressure
description: Emphasize fruits, vegetables, whole grains, beans, and other heart-healthy foods while reducing sodium, especially from processed and restaurant foods.

barrier_addressed: low physical activity
description: Build regular physical activity into daily life to support lower blood pressure, cardiovascular health, and weight management.

intervention_name: Community health worker blood pressure support
actor: community health worker / health system / community organization
barrier_addressed: navigation, trust, follow-up, and self-management barriers
description: Use community health workers to support education, navigation, monitoring, follow-up, and connection to clinical care for people with high blood pressure.

barrier_addressed: high sodium intake from packaged, prepared, or restaurant foods
description: Compare nutrition labels, choose lower-sodium versions when practical, and replace some highly salted foods with less processed options.

barrier_addressed: dietary pattern high in sodium and low in potassium-rich foods
description: Use a DASH-style eating pattern rich in fruits, vegetables, beans, whole grains, and other potassium-containing foods while limiting sodium.

barrier_addressed: persistent stress and limited coping resources
description: Use practical stress-management approaches such as relaxation skills, problem solving, social support, counseling, or other coping strategies that fit the person and situation.

barrier_addressed: stress linked with anxiety, depression, trauma, or impaired daily functioning
description: When stress is persistent or tied to mental health symptoms, connect people with appropriate evaluation and evidence-based mental health support.

barrier_addressed: uncertainty about daily treatment, worsening symptoms, and when to seek help
description: Create a written plan with a health care provider that identifies daily treatment, triggers, warning signs, what to do when symptoms worsen, and when urgent care is needed.

intervention_name: Guideline-based medication review and inhaler education
barrier_addressed: poor symptom control, incorrect inhaler use, or treatment not matched to current asthma severity
description: Review symptom control, prescribed controller and reliever medicines, inhaler technique, adherence barriers, and the treatment plan with a qualified health professional.

intervention_name: Identify and reduce personal asthma triggers
barrier_addressed: repeated exposure to allergens or irritants that worsen symptoms
description: Identify which exposures actually worsen symptoms and use targeted strategies to reduce those exposures while maintaining appropriate medical treatment.

intervention_name: Home-based multi-trigger asthma intervention for children and adolescents
actor: community health worker / nurse / respiratory therapist / public health program
barrier_addressed: multiple indoor triggers plus self-management and navigation barriers
evidence_rating: Community Preventive Services Task Force — strong evidence for children and adolescents
description: Use trained home visitors to assess multiple environmental triggers, provide education, support self-management, and make or coordinate practical environmental changes for children and adolescents with asthma.

intervention_name: Repair moisture sources and remediate mold
actor: resident / landlord / housing program / code enforcement
barrier_addressed: water leaks, persistent dampness, and indoor mold exposure
description: Fix water leaks and moisture sources, dry wet materials promptly, keep indoor humidity controlled, and appropriately clean or remediate mold-contaminated materials.

barrier_addressed: exposure to tobacco smoke where people live and travel
description: Keep homes and vehicles smoke-free and reduce exposure in other indoor spaces. Pair smoke-free rules with cessation support for people who want to stop smoking.

intervention_name: Targeted indoor allergen and pest control
actor: resident / caregiver / housing program / pest-management professional
barrier_addressed: indoor allergens or pests that trigger asthma
description: Use targeted measures based on relevant exposures, such as integrated pest management, dust-mite controls, cleaning, moisture control, and other strategies matched to the person’s known triggers.

actor: individual / caregiver / school / employer / public health agency
barrier_addressed: avoidable exposure during pollution or wildfire-smoke episodes
description: Use local air-quality information to adjust activities and reduce exposure when pollution or wildfire smoke is high, while following the person’s asthma treatment plan.

intervention_name: Follow the Asthma Action Plan for worsening symptoms
barrier_addressed: delayed recognition or treatment of an asthma attack
description: Use the person’s written action plan and prescribed medicines when symptoms worsen, and follow the plan’s instructions for contacting a clinician or seeking urgent or emergency care.

barrier_addressed: undiagnosed high cholesterol
description: Measure cholesterol at appropriate intervals and use overall cardiovascular risk to guide prevention and treatment.

barrier_addressed: dietary patterns that raise LDL cholesterol
description: Emphasize foods lower in saturated and trans fats and support sustainable dietary changes.

barrier_addressed: persistently high LDL or elevated cardiovascular risk
description: Use prescribed cholesterol-lowering medicines when clinically indicated and monitor response and adherence.

barrier_addressed: uncontrolled blood pressure, cholesterol, diabetes, smoking
description: Coordinate control of blood pressure, cholesterol, diabetes, tobacco exposure, activity, and other cardiovascular risks.

barrier_addressed: tobacco exposure
description: Provide counseling, quitline referral, and evidence-based cessation treatment for people who use tobacco.

barrier_addressed: recovery and recurrent cardiovascular risk after qualifying cardiac events
description: Use supervised exercise, education, and risk-factor management after eligible cardiac events or procedures.

barrier_addressed: ongoing tobacco exposure
description: For people who smoke, quitting is the most important step to slow further tobacco-related lung damage.

barrier_addressed: breathlessness, deconditioning, reduced activity
description: Use individualized exercise, education, and self-management training to improve function and quality of life.

barrier_addressed: poor symptom control or inhaler technique
description: Review prescribed inhaled therapies, adherence, technique, symptom control, and exacerbation history.

barrier_addressed: late detection of screen-detectable cancers
description: Offer recommended breast, cervical, colorectal, and lung cancer screening to eligible populations.

barrier_addressed: tobacco-related cancer risk
description: Prevent tobacco initiation and help people who use tobacco quit to reduce risk across multiple cancers.

barrier_addressed: alcohol-related cancer risk
description: Reduce alcohol consumption or avoid alcohol to lower risk for several cancers.

intervention_name: Depression screening with systems for follow-up
barrier_addressed: unrecognized depression
description: Screen adults for depression when systems are in place for accurate diagnosis, treatment, and follow-up.

barrier_addressed: depressive symptoms and impaired functioning
description: Use evidence-based psychotherapy such as cognitive behavioral therapy or interpersonal therapy when appropriate.

barrier_addressed: moderate or severe depression or inadequate response to therapy alone
description: Use antidepressant medication when clinically appropriate with monitoring for effectiveness, adverse effects, and adherence.

barrier_addressed: nicotine dependence and tobacco use
description: Combine behavioral support with appropriate cessation medications and quitline services.

barrier_addressed: dust, fumes, and inhaled workplace hazards
description: Use engineering controls, substitution, ventilation, exposure monitoring, and appropriate respiratory protection to reduce inhaled hazards.

barrier_addressed: limited social support and isolation
description: Increase opportunities for meaningful social connection, supportive relationships, and community participation.

intervention_name: Evaluate persistent thirst and check for diabetes
barrier_addressed: persistent thirst may reflect high blood glucose or another medical cause
description: Persistent or unexplained increased thirst should prompt medical evaluation; diabetes testing may be appropriate depending on symptoms and risk factors.

barrier_addressed: frequent urination may reflect diabetes or other urinary/medical causes
description: Frequent urination that is new, persistent, or paired with thirst, weight loss, or fatigue should be discussed with a clinician and may warrant diabetes testing.

intervention_name: Look for the underlying cause of persistent fatigue
barrier_addressed: fatigue has many possible medical and mental-health causes
description: Persistent or function-limiting fatigue should be evaluated rather than treated as a stand-alone diagnosis; sleep, mood, medications, anemia, diabetes, and other conditions may contribute.

intervention_name: Prompt eye and medical evaluation for new or persistent blurred vision
actor: eye care professional / primary care clinician
barrier_addressed: blurred vision can reflect diabetic eye disease or other urgent eye problems
description: New or persistent blurred vision deserves evaluation, especially in people with diabetes. Sudden major vision loss or severe eye symptoms require urgent care.

intervention_name: Manage glucose, blood pressure, and cholesterol to slow diabetic nerve damage
barrier_addressed: progression of diabetes-related nerve damage
description: For diabetic neuropathy, controlling blood glucose, blood pressure, and cholesterol can help prevent worsening; pain and other symptoms can also be treated clinically.

intervention_name: Daily foot checks and regular foot examinations
barrier_addressed: loss of sensation can allow unnoticed foot injury
description: Check feet daily for cuts, blisters, redness, swelling, or other problems and get regular foot exams, because neuropathy can reduce protective sensation.

intervention_name: Control blood pressure and diabetes and monitor kidney function
actor: primary care / nephrology / diabetes care team
barrier_addressed: progression of chronic kidney disease
description: CKD management centers on blood-pressure control, glucose management when diabetes is present, appropriate medicines, and monitoring kidney function and urine albumin.

barrier_addressed: diet and medicines may need adjustment as kidney function changes
description: A clinician or renal dietitian can tailor sodium, nutrition, and medication plans to kidney function and other conditions.

barrier_addressed: high blood pressure, cholesterol, diabetes, smoking, and inactivity
description: Managing blood pressure, cholesterol, diabetes, tobacco exposure, diet, physical activity, and prescribed medicines lowers cardiovascular risk.

barrier_addressed: limited access to physical activity, healthy food, and preventive care
description: Community strategies that support tobacco cessation, healthy food access, physical activity, and preventive care can reduce shared cardiovascular risk factors.

intervention_name: Recognize stroke signs and call 911 immediately
barrier_addressed: delay in time-sensitive stroke treatment
description: Sudden weakness or numbness, trouble speaking, vision changes, balance problems, or severe unexplained headache can signal stroke. Call 911 immediately; do not drive yourself.

intervention_name: Rehabilitation and secondary prevention after stroke
barrier_addressed: disability and risk of another stroke
description: After stroke, treatment may include rehabilitation plus management of blood pressure, cholesterol, diabetes, heart conditions, medicines, and other risks to reduce recurrence.

intervention_name: Regular dilated eye exams for people with diabetes
barrier_addressed: diabetic retinopathy can progress before symptoms appear
description: People with diabetes should receive regular comprehensive dilated eye exams; early detection and treatment can help prevent vision loss.

barrier_addressed: progressive retinal damage and vision loss
description: Depending on severity, treatment may include eye injections, laser treatment, or surgery, alongside management of diabetes, blood pressure, and cholesterol.

barrier_addressed: small injuries may go unnoticed and become infected
description: Inspect feet every day, keep them clean and protected, and avoid walking barefoot; seek care quickly for sores, redness, swelling, or infection.

intervention_name: Regular professional foot exams and podiatry when needed
barrier_addressed: neuropathy, poor circulation, ulcers, and deformity
description: Regular foot exams help identify loss of sensation, poor circulation, ulcers, and other problems before they become severe.

intervention_name: Use the asthma action plan when wheezing occurs
barrier_addressed: wheezing may signal worsening asthma
description: For people with asthma, follow the individualized Asthma Action Plan, use prescribed medicines correctly, and avoid known triggers.

intervention_name: Seek urgent care for severe breathing symptoms
barrier_addressed: severe asthma can become life-threatening
description: Severe wheezing with major trouble breathing, difficulty talking or walking, or symptoms that do not improve with the action plan can require emergency care.

intervention_name: Assess new or worsening shortness of breath
actor: primary care / urgent or emergency clinician
barrier_addressed: shortness of breath has cardiac, pulmonary, and other causes
description: New, unexplained, or worsening shortness of breath should be medically assessed; sudden severe breathlessness or breathlessness with chest discomfort can be an emergency.

intervention_name: Follow asthma plan for known asthma-related chest tightness
barrier_addressed: chest tightness may indicate worsening asthma
description: If chest tightness is part of a known asthma pattern, follow the prescribed Asthma Action Plan and monitor for worsening symptoms.

intervention_name: Treat unexplained or persistent chest tightness as potentially urgent
barrier_addressed: chest symptoms can overlap with cardiac emergencies
description: New, severe, persistent, or unexplained chest tightness—especially with sweating, nausea, weakness, or shortness of breath—needs urgent evaluation and may require calling 911.

intervention_name: Address the underlying cause of persistent cough
barrier_addressed: cough may reflect asthma, infection, COPD, medications, or other causes
description: A persistent or worsening cough should be evaluated based on its pattern and accompanying symptoms; treatment depends on the underlying cause rather than the cough alone.

intervention_name: Set limits and build alcohol-free days
barrier_addressed: excessive alcohol intake
description: Track drinks, set a limit, schedule alcohol-free days, and reduce situations that trigger heavier drinking. Drinking less is better for health than drinking more.

barrier_addressed: community conditions that encourage excessive alcohol use
evidence_rating: CDC / Community Preventive Services Task Force strategies
description: Population strategies can reduce excessive alcohol use, including approaches affecting alcohol availability, pricing, and retail environments where legally applicable.

intervention_name: Get chest pain diagnosed and follow an individualized angina plan
barrier_addressed: reduced blood flow to heart muscle
description: Angina management may include heart-healthy lifestyle changes, prescribed medicines, cardiac rehabilitation, and procedures when needed.

intervention_name: Call 911 for chest pain that does not go away
barrier_addressed: possible unstable angina or heart attack
description: Chest discomfort that does not go away, is new or markedly worse, or may represent a heart attack should be treated as an emergency and prompt a 911 call.

intervention_name: Call 911 immediately for suspected heart attack
barrier_addressed: delay in restoring blood flow to heart muscle
description: Possible heart attack symptoms require immediate emergency medical care. Call 911 rather than driving yourself; faster treatment can limit heart damage.

barrier_addressed: risk of recurrent cardiovascular events
description: After a heart attack, follow-up care commonly includes medicines, lifestyle changes, and cardiac rehabilitation to reduce the risk of another event.

intervention_name: Create and follow a COPD flare-up plan
actor: person with COPD / pulmonary care team
barrier_addressed: delayed treatment of worsening COPD symptoms
description: People with COPD should discuss a flare-up plan with their clinician so they know how to respond to worsening breathlessness, cough, or sputum changes and when to seek care.

intervention_name: Pulmonary rehabilitation after or between exacerbations when appropriate
barrier_addressed: breathlessness, reduced function, and recurrent symptoms
description: Pulmonary rehabilitation combines supervised exercise, education, and breathing strategies and can improve function and quality of life for appropriate patients with COPD.

intervention_name: Use evidence-based insomnia treatment for persistent sleep problems
actor: primary care / sleep clinician / behavioral health clinician
barrier_addressed: chronic insomnia and poor sleep quality
description: For chronic insomnia, cognitive behavioral therapy for insomnia (CBT-I) is usually recommended as the first treatment option; regular sleep habits are also part of treatment.

intervention_name: Evaluate persistent sleep disturbance for underlying causes
barrier_addressed: sleep problems may arise from medical, mental-health, behavioral, or environmental causes
description: Persistent sleep problems deserve evaluation when they impair daytime function or continue despite basic sleep-habit changes.

intervention_name: Seek evaluation if concentration problems persist or impair daily life
barrier_addressed: concentration problems may reflect mood, sleep, medication, neurological, or other causes
description: Difficulty concentrating that is severe, persistent, or interfering with work, school, or daily tasks should be discussed with a clinician rather than assumed to have a single cause.
